`p` in main receives the pointer value that the function will return.

steps.title: Dangerous return - address of local variable
steps.explanation:
`return &x;` returns the address of a local variable that will soon be destroyed.

After the function ends, the address becomes a dangling pointer with no valid target.

steps.title: Dangling Pointer Dereference - Undefined Behavior
steps.explanation:
The moment you read `*p`, the behavior is Undefined Behavior.

The values ​​may appear to be correct by chance, may produce garbage values, or may crash, so they are not reliable.

quiz.question: What is a safe way to return data generated from a function?
options: Returns the address of a local variable
Returns a static variable or malloc (dynamically allocated) address.
Print and exit with printf inside the function.
quiz.explanation: `static` variables are stored in the data area and `malloc` are stored in the heap area, so they do not disappear when the function ends.

misconceptions.wrong: In C language, a compilation error does not occur even if you return &x.
misconceptions.correct: In most cases, they just give a warning and move on.
misconceptions.why:
So, this is one of the most common mistakes beginners make.
Never ignore the "Address of stack memory associated with local variable 'x' returned" warning.

keyTakeaway: Never export the address (&local) of a local variable that will disappear.
